title: Mohammad Akraminia, the Iranian army Spokesperson:
text:
Mohammad Akraminia, the Iranian army Spokesperson:"

""

"Mohammad Akraminia, spokesman for the Iranian army: "A change in military doctrine is about to be established, and thank God, this change in military doctrine has been implemented today, and its effects have become apparent. I will present the signs of this to you. One of the signs of this change is the rapid response; of course, we responded rapidly from the very beginning of the war. You observed that we responded immediately two hours after the start of the U.S. aggression on Feb 27th. This is one of the components of the change in military doctrine—from defense to offense, and we have moved this military doctrine toward an offensive military doctrine.""

"Mohammad Akraminia, spokesman for the Iranian army: "The evolutionary process and transformation of the military doctrine of the Armed Forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran is an ongoing and continuous matter that is progressing toward perfection. Indeed, the operations carried out by our pilots on March 1st, both the attack on the Buehring base [Kuwait] by F-5s and the attack on the US base in Qatar by Su-24s, demonstrates the offensive approach of the Army of the Islamic Republic of Iran.""

"Mohammad Akraminia, spokesman for the Iranian army: "If the enemy hit one of our points, we had to provide a more crushing response in places where it was necessary, not everywhere now, but in places where we truly felt that if this action were not taken, the enemy would actually become more emboldened. For example, attacks on infrastructure. If you recall, during the war, the enemy hit some points of our petrochemical and energy infrastructures; at the same moment a point of ours was targeted, we targeted several points. This in itself demonstrates that offensive approach in the new military doctrine of the Islamic Republic of Iran.""

"Mohammad Akraminia, spokesman for the Iranian army: "In addition to the expansion of geography, new topics will also arise in the potential future war. Consider the energy infrastructures in the region and the communication infrastructures in the region, which primarily pass through the floor of the Persian Gulf and the Sea of Oman; these communication infrastructures, and anywhere the enemy has interests, could become legitimate targets for the armed forces of the Islamic Republic of Iran in the future. This means entering new arenas of war should the enemy, in fact, make a miscalculation.
